statement: Let \(ABCDE\) be a regular pentagon. The star \(ACEBD\) has area \(1\). Lines \(AC\) and \(BE\) meet at \(P\), while lines \(BD\) and \(CE\) meet at \(Q\). Find the area of \(APQD\).
Show that if \(\sqrt{2}\) is written in decimal notation, there is at least one nonzero digit among the digits in positions \(1{,}000{,}000\) through \(3{,}000{,}000\).

How many coins can be placed on a \(10 \times 10\) board (at most one per square, each at the center of its square) so that no four coins form a rectangle with sides parallel to the sides of the board?

On planet Zork there are some cities, and for every city there is one at the diametrically opposite point. Roads join certain pairs of cities; if there is a road between \(P\) and \(Q\), there is also one between their antipodal cities \(P'\) and \(Q'\). The roads do not cross, and any two cities are connected by a path. The Kriptonita prices in two cities connected by a road differ by at most \(100\) Urghs. Prove that there exist two diametrically opposite cities whose Kriptonita prices differ by at most \(100\) Urghs.

There are \(n\) football teams in Tumbolia. A round-robin championship is organised in which each team plays every other team exactly once, every match takes place on a Sunday, and each team plays at most one match per Sunday. Find the least positive integer \(m_n\) for which it is possible to set up such a championship lasting \(m_n\) Sundays.

Given any triangle \(ABC\), construct \(A'\) on side \(AB\), \(B'\) on side \(BC\), and \(C'\) on side \(CA\) such that triangles \(ABC\) and \(A'B'C'\) are similar (with \(\angle A = \angle A'\), \(\angle B = \angle B'\), \(\angle C = \angle C'\)) and \(A'B'C'\) has the least possible area.
